text: More than 1,400 years ago, a merchant named Muhammad lived in Mecca, a trading town in Arabia.
According to Islamic tradition, God sent him messages through the angel Gabriel while he sat in quiet thought in a cave.
src: 610 to today / Islam began in Mecca, a trading town in western Arabia / Muhammad, born there around 570 into the clan of Hashim of the tribe of Quraysh, was orphaned young and worked as a merchant
According to Islamic tradition, around 610, while meditating in a cave on Mount Hira, he received the first of a series of revelations from God through the angel Gabriel

text: Muslims believe these messages are the word of God, gathered in their holy book, the Quran.
They believe there is only one God, and that Muhammad is God’s messenger, the last of the prophets.
src: The Quran, “the recitation”, is for Muslims the literal word of God / These revelations, recited by him and memorised and written down by his followers, form the Quran
There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the messenger of God / Muhammad is the last of them, the “seal of the prophets”

text: Within a hundred years, the caliphs, Muhammad’s successors, ruled lands from Spain to Central Asia.
Later, traders, scholars and Sufis carried Islam across Africa, India and Southeast Asia.
src: Within a century of Muhammad’s death in 632 the caliphs ruled from Spain to Central Asia / caliph, “successor”
traders, scholars and Sufis later carried Islam across Africa, India and Southeast Asia

text: Muslims divided into two main groups, Sunni and Shia, over who should lead the community after Muhammad.
For Shia Muslims, the shrines at Najaf and Karbala are important places of pilgrimage.
src: Divided since the first century into Sunni and Shia traditions / The question of who should lead the community after Muhammad shaped Islamic history
for Shia Muslims, the shrines of the imams at Najaf, Karbala and Mashhad are centres of pilgrimage

text: Scholars writing in Arabic made advances in maths, astronomy and medicine, and builders made palaces like the Alhambra.
Even English words like algebra, coffee and sugar came from Arabic.
src: scholars working in Arabic preserved and translated Greek philosophy and science and made advances of their own in mathematics, with al-Khwarizmi’s algebra; in astronomy, optics and medicine / the Alhambra of Granada
Arabic, the language of the Quran / gave words to Persian, Turkish, Swahili, Urdu, Malay and, through them and through Spain, to English: algebra, alcohol, admiral, coffee and sugar among them

text: Today about 2 billion people are Muslims, and Indonesia has more of them than any other country.
They pray five times a day, give to the poor, fast in Ramadan and, if they can, make the journey to Mecca.
src: About 2 billion (2020), the second-largest religion; the largest Muslim country is Indonesia

the five daily prayers / zakat, the giving of a share of one’s wealth to the poor; fasting from dawn to sunset during the month of Ramadan; and the hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, which every Muslim who is able should make once in a lifetime
